result.summary: This PR raises the minimum C++ standard for Bitcoin Core from C++20 to C++23 in CMake, depends, and CI environments, requiring GCC 13 or Clang 19. It removes internal polyfills and workarounds—migrating util::Expected to std::expected, adopting std::byteswap, and removing the ALWAYS_FALSE type trait—and applies C++23 features such as std::string::contains and std::views::zip across the codebase.
result.problem: Targeting C++20 requires maintaining custom polyfills, template workarounds, and older idioms in tree, even as related external dependencies like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features.
evidence: Author notes in description: 'the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes'
Author notes in description that switching compiler standards unlocks future work tracked in #34979
result.scope_notes: This is an RFC/draft PR. In addition to build system changes bumping compiler requirements to GCC 13+ and Clang 19+, it includes mechanical replacements of .find() with .contains() across over 50 files and replaces util::Expected with std::expected.
result.changed_since_previous: Minor adjustments to pass Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) checks and adjustments to unit tests for std::expected compatibility.
result.card: This pull request bumps the project's minimum C++ standard from C++20 to C++23, raising compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19 across CMake, depends, and CI. It replaces internal polyfills with standard library equivalents (std::expected and std::byteswap), removes template workarounds like ALWAYS_FALSE, and modernizes string searches with std::string::contains across 56 files. The author argues that workarounds to avoid C++23 continue to accumulate while related libraries like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features. This PR is an RFC draft and unblocks work tracked in #34979.

risk.why: Bumping the minimum compiler version and standard library requirements across all platforms could break compilation on older supported distributions or introduce subtle toolchain regressions into release binaries.
